source.name: A non-modal offcanvas panel that allows page scrolling must not trap keyboard focus
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/pull/33677) at 0bbe45cd977ae69f11b4cdd55e5d5be08e4a137a. Blind to the maintainers' fix 079f2cd90c247225eb71dff4d514faf50f653416; routing auto.

journey.title: Keep editing the report with the help panel open
journey.goal: Tab can reach the amount field while the non-modal panel is open

functionalJourney.title: Open and close the policy help panel
functionalJourney.goal: The panel opens and its close button hides it

guards.title: Close the help panel from the keyboard
guards.goal: The panel's close button is reachable and closes it

plan.root_cause: The offcanvas plugin adds a focus-in listener that returns focus to the panel whenever focus leaves it, making the help panel modal and preventing tab navigation to the amount field.
plan.repair_strategy: Remove the focus enforcement call in the shown callback of the offcanvas show method, allowing focus to move beyond the panel while preserving other attributes.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Users can tab from the help panel's close button to the amount field when the panel is open, meeting the focus order requirement.
functional_risks: Removing focus trapping may allow focus to wander into background elements if the panel were intended to be modal, but the panel is designed as non‑modal.
Assistive technologies may still perceive the panel as modal due to aria-modal and role attributes, but keyboard behavior aligns with a non‑modal panel.
verification_requirements: After opening the help panel, pressing Tab moves focus to the help-close button and then to the amount field within two tab presses.
Shift+Tab moves focus back from the amount field to the help-close button and then to the open-help button.
The help panel can still be closed via its close button and via the Escape key (if keyboard:true).
The panel's visibility, aria-modal, and role attributes remain unchanged.
